item: Run records for the legacy single-file restore, the newsletter folder import and the folder backup, restore and verify, told apart by a fixed-table via; the folder verify's counts, always empty, fixed; an unexaminable path is a recorded refusal; the slot goes from 115,000 to 125,000 bytes
summary: The run records of the volume backup, restore and verify were joined by the paths the first entry named as not recorded: restore_legacy_path, the newsletter import worker and the FolderBackupManager workers write a run OPEN, close it at every branch and in a finally net, and record a refused start at the raise, into the same three kinds. Every run carries via (volume-set, single-file, newsletter-eml, folder), a key of a fixed table. A path the system cannot examine (a name too long, a denied parent) is a refusal with the key path-unreadable and the class name, and the error the caller saw is unchanged; it is recorded by a net (run_refusals_net) round the start's header that reads only the class of what leaves, so the six path-check statements stay exactly as main has them (not a changed line of the diff); a free-space figure that cannot be read is free-space-unreadable and never a shortage. New numbers: files, files_done, resumed_from, copied, skipped, restored, checked, mismatches. The folder verify's closing line had always recorded None because it read keys the verifier does not return; one _verify_counts now feeds both journals. The cancel flag is read once per worker. The legacy stop is asked with issubclass(type(exc), ...) so the passphrase AST guard holds. The slot is 125,000 bytes (widest journal 116,930, ordinary names 72,220; free room 1,613,784 against a pin of 1,500,000). 23 mutants of the fold each killed by a named test; ruff advisory total 416 (ceiling 417), mypy clean.
